findings.claim: Eval row r2 required a pre-apply dump that was never taken.
The page dropped the devcontainer caveat on the x509 spike, and the paragraph had semicolon splices.

null_resource.bifrost_ready can pass against the old allocation. nomad_job.bifrost keeps the provider default detach = true, so the apply goes on as soon as Nomad accepts the job, and the /health poll can reach the 2.6.0 gateway before it stops. The 2.7.0 apply showed this: the gate passed, then the gateway refused connections for about a minute. The comment on the gate says virtual keys are only touched after the gateway is back up, which is not true. This change did not cause it, and this round changed no key. nomad_job.openviking already uses detach = false for the same reason.

verdict.text: The change is ready to commit.
Bifrost is pinned to 2.7.0, the pin test moved with it, and the component page records the operator's no-dump decision and the correct one-way migrations for both steps.
The gates pass and the live gateway runs 2.7.0 and passes the smoke checks.
Both round-1 findings are resolved.
The one new finding is a readiness race that was already there before this change.
It does not block.
Diff: the worktree changes are uncommitted against HEAD 0ee1dc51, and HEAD matches main outside `.loop/`.
I read all three changed files.
`services.tf` changes one line (`bifrost_version = "2.7.0"`).
`providers.tf` is untouched (`~>0.1.0`).
Gates: `loopctl gate stamp` printed `pass gate pre_commit`, `pass gate cli_tests`, `pass eval-row r1`, `stamp green: 9bba4978b031c123e4b6123ee54190f475ed65c046c364479614ad87c67e197c`.

r1: the test asserts the pin list equals exactly `["2.7.0"]`, the `~>0.1.0` provider constraint, and that the smoke script still expects `access_not_found` and no longer expects `virtual_key_not_found`.
Every clause of fails_when would fail it.

r2 (judgment): the page says the operator chose no dump, that there is no restore point to 2.3.1, that 2.6.0 to 2.7.0 adds eight migrations, six of which can be undone, and it names both one-way migrations.
It says there is no way back to 2.6.0 without a dump.
It claims no rollback path.
The names match plan step 3 and the plan-review round 4 check against the release notes.
Passes.
r3 (judgment): I re-ran `scripts/bifrost_smoke.py` against 192.168.2.50:8080.
It printed gateway "v2.7.0" and ok on all five checks.
`nomad job inspect` shows image `docker.io/maximhq/bifrost:v2.7.0`, and deployment 78c9f536 is successful.
I accept the implementer's recorded evidence for the rerank (200, [0.999, 0.024]), the Gemini chat (200) and the second plan (only `nomad_job.hermes`, no `bifrost_virtual_key`).
That hermes diff comes from hermes-update-0-23 being live from its own worktree and not yet on main.
Passes.
r4 (judgment): the page's lead names v2.7.0 and the latency note is present.
A grep of `docs/` and `.okf/` turns up 2.3.1 only in history (hermes.md, ADR 0029, a handoff, log.md).
No page names 2.3.1 or 2.6.0 as current.
Passes.
The readiness observation: I read `null_resource.bifrost_ready` and `nomad_job.bifrost`.
See f3.
f1: resolved.
The operator re-signed r2 under grant g10 to record the no-dump choice.
The page at `.okf/components/bifrost.md` (new version-history paragraph) now states that choice and the fact that neither 2.3.1 nor 2.6.0 can be restored.
f2: resolved.
The spike paragraph now says the x509 result was "seen from the devcontainer rather than the cluster nodes", and that only Gemini was called live after the apply.
The latency sentence no longer uses a semicolon.
One semicolon is left before "after the apply Gemini answered".
The slop rule treats that as low confidence, so I leave it to the author.
f3: open, hardening, not blocking.
The gate can see the old allocation because the bifrost job is not applied with `detach = false`.
The fix is to add `detach = false` to `nomad_job.bifrost`, as `nomad_job.openviking` already has, or to have the gate check the version the gateway reports.
Either fix also makes the gate's comment true.
This was already broken before this ticket.
No virtual key changed this round, so nothing was harmed here.
It belongs in a follow-up ticket.
The pin test's docstring names only the 2.3.1 to 2.6.0 migrations as one-way.
That is still true, but the pin is now 2.7.0, whose two one-way migrations it does not mention.
I am not asking for a change.
The minute of refused connections during the restart is what a single-allocation job does on redeploy, and the plan accepts it.
The only problem is the gate reporting ready too early, which is f3.
